purpose: Exploratory card-detail layouts; no implementation or approved design decision.

concepts.label: A — Relation cards beside the reading view
concepts.prompt:
Create a landscape UI wireframe image, a clear design artifact for the open-backlog application, NOT application code. Match the attached reference's clean grayscale wireframe treatment: white/off-white surfaces, fine gray borders, readable sans-serif typography, restrained corner rounding, dark text. The reference is STYLE ONLY; create the new detail-view composition described below. No colour palette, gradients, photos, 3D, illustrations or decorative graphics. Use a generous landscape canvas around 1600 by 1100. Prioritise readable text and convincingly sized UI controls. Show a faint dimmed backlog board as contextual background behind a single large detail workspace; its background is not interactive.

All concepts use the same clearly illustrative data, not the repository's actual items:
Parent epic: "W-60  Checkout refresh", progress "2 of 6 done".
Six epic members, in this order:
"W-61  Order summary" — "Done".
"W-62  Address form" — "Done".
"W-63  Payment errors" — "In progress"; this is the selected member, mark its microcard with a strong outline AND the word "Viewing".
"W-64  Confirmation" — "Ready".
"W-65  Receipt email" — "Waiting on W-63".
"W-66  Checkout review" — "Ready".
Each microcard is a small bordered clickable tile with readable ID, a short title, a text state, and a subtle directional affordance. No image thumbnails. Do not make microcards look like disabled chips. Indicate clickability with structure, not giant pointers. Do not use colour as the only status or selected signal.

The selected detail view contains the heading "W-63  Payment errors", compact metadata "In progress", "High priority", "Build", "Checkout", and reading content:
"Why"
"Make failures clear and recoverable."
"Acceptance"
"Explain what failed"
"Keep entered details"
"Offer a clear retry".
There are "Copy prompt", "Open file", and a visible Close control. Keep a comfortable reading width and an obvious return link to the parent epic. Draw actual text, not gibberish or skeleton lines, but avoid adding extra long prose. These images explore navigating relationships INSIDE the detail workspace: selecting a microcard replaces the main detail content, with the epic context preserved. Do not show stacked item dialogs or several selected items. Preserve distinct relationship groups; a dependency is not the same as a related item.

COMPOSITION A: Label the image at the top "A / Related cards". Beneath this title, show a large centred detail dialog with the selected item's reading column taking about two thirds of its width. The right-hand third is a tidy relationship sidebar. At the top of the sidebar, under "In this epic", put one microcard for "W-60  Checkout refresh" and its "2 of 6 done" progress. Then group smaller microcards under the exact headings "Depends on" (W-61 Order summary, Done; W-62 Address form, Done), "Unblocks" (W-65 Receipt email, Waiting on W-63), and "Related" (W-66 Checkout review, Ready). Make those group headings easy to distinguish. The left reading column should have roomy prose and a compact set of editable-looking field dropdowns above it. A small breadcrumb links back to Checkout refresh. Keep the dialog's Close and action controls in the top bar. Show a restrained caption at the bottom: "Select a small card to open it here." This option is about understanding connections while reading a single item.

W-63 Payment errors is strongly outlined and marked "Viewing"; it is third, not first. The large right panel shows only W-63's title, metadata and Why/Acceptance content. Caption: "Move through the epic without losing your place." This is the main concept for fast epic navigation and must feel simple, spatially stable, and readable.

W-63 has a strong outline and "Viewing". Give every microcard enough room for its title and text state. The right-hand reading pane replaces its content when selecting a different microcard; the epic grid stays. Place "Previous member" and "Next member" below it. Caption: "Keep the whole epic in view while inspecting one item." Distinguish this from a list rail: the epic summary and compact tile grid are the visual anchors.

concepts.label: Phone — Browse the epic and read a member
concepts.prompt:
Create one landscape design image containing TWO phone-sized wireframes side by side, in the exact clean grayscale wireframe style of the attached reference. This is for open-backlog's card-detail and epic navigation design, not application code. White/off-white surfaces, fine gray borders, dark readable sans-serif text, no colour, no photos, no gradients, no tiny desktop UI crammed into a phone. Title the image "Epic navigation on a phone". Use the same illustrative epic "W-60  Checkout refresh", progress "2 of 6 done", six members: W-61 Order summary / Done; W-62 Address form / Done; W-63 Payment errors / In progress; W-64 Confirmation / Ready; W-65 Receipt email / Waiting on W-63; W-66 Checkout review / Ready.
LEFT PHONE: label it "Browse epic". A full-screen detail view with Close at top right, the parent epic title and 2 of 6 done progress, then a two-column-by-three-row grid of six genuinely tappable microcards. Every microcard has its ID, title and text state. W-63 is strongly outlined and labelled "Viewing". Below show a short epic description and a "Copy epic prompt" button. No additional sidebar.
RIGHT PHONE: label it "Read member". A full-screen item detail with a clear "Back to Checkout refresh" link and Close, heading "W-63  Payment errors", state "In progress", and "Item 3 of 6". Directly below, two small but comfortably tappable navigation cards: "Previous member / W-62 Address form / Done" and "Next member / W-64 Confirmation / Ready". A full-width text button "View all 6 items" returns to the epic browser. Under this navigation area show "Why", "Make failures clear and recoverable.", "Acceptance", and three short checkbox-like bullets "Explain what failed", "Keep entered details", "Offer a clear retry". Include Copy prompt and Open file actions. All touch targets should appear at least about 2.75rem tall at normal phone scale. Caption below both phones: "Tap a microcard to switch items; return to the epic in one step." Make the return path and the current selection obvious. This is a pair of navigation states, not two dialogs stacked over one another.

revisions.purpose: Correct the parent epic progress indicator to exactly six segments with two done.
revisions.prompt: Edit this UI wireframe with ONE precise change. In the small parent epic microcard at the upper right, under the title 'W-60 Checkout refresh' and beside the text '2 of 6 done', replace the small progress bar with EXACTLY SIX equal-width, clearly separated segments. The first TWO segments are dark gray to represent W-61 and W-62 being done, and the remaining FOUR segments are light gray. Keep the text '2 of 6 done'. Preserve everything else: the entire composition, canvas size, all wording, dialog and sidebar, the bottom six epic member microcards, the Viewing marker on W-63, the muted board background, borders, typography and grayscale treatment. Do not redraw other parts or add anything. This is a correction to a progress count, not a redesign.
